Add the chicken pieces and apricots to the sauce, reduce the heat to a simmer and cook, partially covered, for 35 â 40 minutes or until the chicken is cooked through. Remove the cinnamon stick.
To serve, sprinkle the chopped coriander and almonds over the chicken.

ing: salt and freshly ground black pepper
st: Heat the butter in a large frying pan, then add the garlic and onion and sautÃ© for 2 â 3 minutes until just softened.
Add the lemon juice and zest and reduce to half.
Add the cream and capers and cook for 5 minutes until the cream has thickened. Stir through the Italian parsley and season to taste.
Heat another pan with the olive oil on a medium heat.
Add the pork schnitzels and fry for about 5 minutes on each side or until golden brown and cooked through.
Serve the warm schnitzels with the cream sauce poured over.

ing: salt and freshly ground black pepper
1 x 800 g Italian whole peeled tomatoes
st: Heat the olive oil in a heavy-bottomed pot over a high heat and brown the pork on all sides. Remove from the pot and set aside.
Add the onion to the pot and cook until lightly golden and softened, about 5 minutes.
Add the garlic, curry powder and cumin and stir-fry for 1 minute.
Add the chicken stock, red wine, bay leaves, tomatoes and sugar and bring to the boil.
Add the potatoes and simmer for about 20 minutes until the sauce has thickened and the potatoes are tender.
Place the pork back in the pot and cook for a further 10 minutes or until the meat is just cooked through.
Remove the bay leaves, stir in the parsley and season to taste.

ing: 400 g Woolworths frozen all-butter puff pastry
st: Preheat the oven to 180Â°C. Place the pastry on a floured surface and cut into 3 rectangles.
Squeeze the sausage meat out of the casings and roll into 3 long sausages. Place one in the centre of each pastry sheet.
Using a pastry brush, brush the pastry on either side of the sausage meat with the beaten egg. Pinch the egg-washed sides together to encase the sausage rolls.
Cut each one into 5 equal pieces and place on a greased baking tray.
Bake for 15â20 minutes, or until golden brown. Serve with the minty salsa.

ing: 50 g peanuts, lightly toasted, for serving
2 x 100 g Woolworths medium rice noodles, cooked according to package instructions
500 g Woolworths frozen fully cooked shell-on prawns
1 lime, juiced, plus 2 extra for serving
st: To make the curry paste, heat the oil in a pan over a medium heat. Add the spring onions, chilli and garlic and cook for a few seconds. Remove from the heat and mix in the tamarind paste, shrimp paste, fish sauce, lime juice and palm sugar.
Return to the heat and cook for a further 2 minutes. Remove from the heat and allow to cool.
Heat a little oil in a nonstick frying pan over a medium heat. Whisk the eggs and pour into the pan, making a thin omelette. Cook until set, then set aside.

Heat the coconut oil in a pan over medium to high heat and fry the prawns until golden. Mix in the curry paste and add the noodles. Toss in the bean sprouts, peanuts and chopped omelette. Garnish with coriander, onion sprinkles and wedges of lime.
Cook the pumpkin in a saucepan of boiling, salted water until tender, then drain well.
Mash the pumpkin using a fork and add the eggs, psyllium husks, nutmeg, chilli flakes and salt.

Dust a work surface with coconut or almond flour and spoon equal quantities of mashed pumpkin onto the surface. Flatten the pumpkin until 2 mm thick using the palm of your hand. Ensure that each tortilla is completely covered in flour and dry and pliable.
Heat a pan oven a medium heat and dry fry the tortillas for 3 minutes on each side, or until golden brown.

ing: sea salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
1 x 240 g packet Woolworths sundried tomatoes
st: Preheat the oven to 200Â°C. Add the sundried tomatoes, chilli flakes, paprika, garlic, red peppers, oregano olive oil, lemon juice or vinegar to a pan and season to taste.
Simmer for 10 minutes, remove from the heat and blend until smooth.

Carefully lift the skin of the chicken and spread a couple of tablespoons of the sauce underneath without tearing the skin. Spread another few tablespoons on top, dot with butter and drizzle with olive oil.
Season and roast on a tray of sliced potatoes for 35â40 minutes, basting every 10 minutes.\

ing: 2 tbsp Woolworths almond nut butter spread
2 heaped  tbsp cocoa powder, plus extra for dusting
2 tbsp Woolworths almond nut butter spread
st: Add the nuts to a blender along with the almond nut butter and it smooth a paste. For the cocoa nut butter bombs: add the cocoa and blend through. Shape small balls of the mixture before rolling in extra cocoa to coat.
For the coconut nut butter bombs, repeat the process but instead of adding the cocoa add the coconut instead before blending then roll in more coconut to coat.
Store the nut butter bombs in the fridge or freezer.

ing: sea salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
sea salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
st: Preheat the oven to 180Â°C. Heat the butter in a large, non-stick pan overa medium heat.
Whisk the eggs, salt and pepper. Pour the egg mixture into the pan and cook, gently moving the mixture with a spatula, for 5 minutes. Finish in the oven for 10 minutes, or until puffed up and golden.
To make the topping, heat the butter in a pan over a medium to high heat. SautÃ© the spinach and herbs with the salt and pepper for 5 minutes, or until tender.
To assemble, flip the frittata ontoa plate and top with the spinach mixture.

ing: sea salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
60 g Woolworths fresh baby herb leaves
100 g rhubarb, sliced with a vegetable peeler
st: To make the pickled Romanesco, heat the water, sugar, vinegar and salt until dissolved. Allow to cool.
Break the Romanesco into pieces, place in a bowl and pour over the vinegar. Allow to cool.
To assemble, place the baby leaf salad, rhubarb and spelt in a bowl and toss with half the dressing.
Pile the salad onto a platter and stud with the pickled Romanesco.
Scatter with the microleaf salad and walnuts and drizzle over the remaining dressing.

ing: sea salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
st: Soften the onion, garlic and rosemary in the oil for 5 minutes over a low heat.
Increase the heat, add the pork mince and brown for 5 minutes.
Stir in the tomatoes and tomato paste, season and cook for 10 minutes. Add the cream and cook for a further 5 minutes.
Serve with the Parmesan and chilli on ciabatta rolls,al dentepenne or cooked baby marrow spaghetti.

ing: 1/2 red chilli, finely chopped (optional if you're cooking for kids)
sea salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
st: Heat the oil in a pan over a medium heat.
Pan-fry the mince until brown. Add the cumin, smoked paprika, coriander and season to taste.
Add the onion, garlic, red pepper and chilli to the pan.
Simmer for 15 minutes â if the mixture is too dry, add the chicken stock.
Blanch the sweetcorn in salted boiling water until tender, then char on a griddle pan.
Serve the mince and corn with sour cream and ready-made guacamole.
Garnish with spring onion.

ing: 500 g lamb mince, at room temperature
salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
a handful parsley, chopped, for sprinkling
1 x 400 g can chopped Italian tomatoes
st: Lightly brown the onion in 2 T olive oil. Stir in the spices and crushed garlic, then remove from the pan and mix with the mince. Add the egg, couscous and salt to the spiced mince and mix.
Shape the mince into balls, it should make about 12 to 14 balls. Brown in 1 T olive oil.

Pour off any remaining oil, then add the tomatoes and chicken stock to the pan containing the lamb patties. Cover and cook gently for 15 minutes, or until cooked through. Check the seasoning and sprinkle with parsley.
Ladle into large bowls and serve with the vegetable couscous and hot sauce.

To make the vegetable couscous, bring the stock and vegetables to a boil. Simmer briskly for 2 to 3 minutes. Stir in the couscous, cover tightly and turn off the heat. Leave for 5 to 10 minutes. Stir through with a large fork and check seasoning.

ing: 100 g black kalamata olives, pitted and quartered
sea salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
sea salt and freshly ground pepper, to taste
st: Preheat the oven to 200Â°C. Coat the peppers in 2 T olive oil and place, skin-side up, on a baking tray. Roast for 15 to 20 minutes until the skin blisters. Transfer to a bowl and cover with clingwrap. Set aside.
In a large mixing bowl, combine the lamb mince, red onion, oregano and seasoning. Divide the mixture into 8 equal portions and shape into small patties. Chill for 30 minutes.
Fry the patties in the remaining oil for 2 minutes on each side. Transfer to a baking tray and finish in the oven for 4 minutes.
Toast the bread rolls on a hot grill pan until golden. Meanwhile, remove the skins from the roasted peppers.

To make the tzatziki, use a vegetable peeler to slice the cucumbers into thin ribbons. Combine the cucumber, yoghurt, and lemon juice and zest in a mixing bowl. Season to taste and chill until ready to assemble.

To assemble the burgers, spread a generous layer of hummus on half a grilled roll. Top with roasted peppers, a lamb patty and a dollop of tzatziki. Finish with black olive salsa, a sprig of fresh coriander and the remaining half of the roll.

ing: 4 Woolworths brown seeded rolls, lightly toasted
200 g lean back bacon, grilled until lightly crisp
sea salt and freshly ground pepper, to taste
st: Add the burger patties to a mixing bowl, scatter in the parmesan and combine the cheese into the meat. Reshape into 4 equal sized patties.
Heat the oil over a medium heat before adding the patties and frying for 2-3 minutes or until well caramelized. Turn over and cook the other side in the same way.

Place the base of the base of the buns to a serving platter before adding the watercress, and scattering of red onion. Top with the burger patty then add some jalapeno and avocado then finish of with a squeeze of lime, seasoning and topping with the last half of the bun.

ing: 100 g Woolworths Roasted and salted luxury tree nut
st: In a mixing bowl combine the mascarpone cream cheese, lemon zest, chilli flakes and onion sprinkle.

Over a sheet of cling wrap, scatter the nut sprinkle, then add the cheese mixture in a sausage like shape before rolling carefully to coat in the nut sprinkle. Wrap tightly in the cling-wrap and shape into 1 large sausage. Keep in the fridge to set.
Unwrap and serve when needed with Woolworths 3 cheese straws.

ing: a handful fresh coriander, finely chopped
2.5 cm piece ginger, peeled and chopped
1 pineapple, skin and core removed, then roughly chopped
st: Process the fish sauce, pineapple, garlic, ginger, brown sugar and soya sauce in a blender.
Marinate the trout for 30 minutes to 1 hour in half of the pineapple mixture. Reserve the remaining mixture for serving.
For the onion pickle, bring a saucepan of lightly salted water to a boil over a high heat.
Add the sliced red onion, blanch it for 30 seconds, then drain it well.
In a small bowl, whisk together the rice wine vinegar, white sugar and a Â¼ teaspoon of sea salt flakes.
Add the drained onion and stir to combine.
Set aside to pickle at room temperature for at least 20 minutes, stirring occasionally.
For the salsa, whisk the coriander, olive oil, lime juice, lime zest and the remaining teaspoon of sea salt flakes in a medium bowl.
Heat the grill and cook the trout to your liking.
Mix the cubed avocado and mango with the coriander dressing.
Drain the pickled onions, scatter them over the salsa and serve with the grilled trout, topped with remaining pineapple mixture.

ing: 4 Woolworths heat and eat garlic naan breads, prepared as instructed
extra virgin olive oil, for drizzling
4 tbsp fresh coriander leaves, roughly chopped
st: Using a griddle pan or under the oven grill.
Heat the griddle pan over a high heat. Drizzle some olive oil over the espetadas then add to the oven, turning every 5 minutes
Once the belly is perfectly cooked and slightly charred remove the espetadas from the oven and allow to cool slightly before serving.

For the pickled butternut spaghetti: Heat the vinegar, sugar, red chilli, and fennel seeds together over a medium heat while stirring until all the sugar has dissolved. Remove from the heat and add the butternut. Stir to coat the butternut and allow to cool.
Add the naan bread to a serving platter and spread some yoghurt over before scattering some coriander over. Add some of the pork as well as some of the carrots.

ing: 2 x 250 g tubs plain full-cream cream cheese
100 g blueberries, plus extra to garnish
st: Grease a round 24 cm loose-bottomed tart tin with a little oil.
Place the biscuits in a food processor and blitz until fine, or crush in a bag. Transfer to a bowl and mix in the butter.
Press the biscuit mixture firmly into the greased tart tin, and up the sides. Chill for 20 minutes.
To make the filling, beat the cream cheese until smooth and gradually add the condensed milk. Mix until well incorporated. Fold in the lemon zest.
Spoon the filling evenly into the tart tin. Chill for 1 hour.
Place the blueberries, lemon juice and sugar in a saucepan over a medium to high heat and cook for 5 minutes, or until soft and juicy.
When ready to serve, remove the cheesecake from the fridge and gently push the out of the tin. Garnish with the glazed blueberries, berries and plums.

t: Open chicken and roast veg pie
ing: sea salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
200 g leftover roast chicken or turkey
300 g leftover roast vegetables (cubed butternut, red onion)
1 sheet Woolworths all-butter puff pastry sheet, thawed
st: Preheat the oven to 200Â°C.

Score a 2 cm border around the puff pastry to create a crust. Place on a baking tray. 2 Brush with the beaten egg, taking care not to let any egg drip off the sides as this will stop the pastry from rising. Bake for 10 minutes.

Meanwhile, soften the leeks in the olive oil for 5 minutes over a low heat, then add the garlic and leftover roast vegetables, chicken or turkey and half the gravy. Sprinkle over the thyme and season to taste.
Spoon onto the pastry sheet and return to the oven for 5â10 minutes. Serve hot with the remaining gravy and a handful of rocket.
Melt 200 g sugar in a pan until golden brown, then pour onto baking paper to make a thin disc of caramel.
Sprinkle with 100 g chopped pecan nuts and a good pinch of crushed pink peppercorns while still hot, then allow to cool completely to set.
Crush over ripe Camembert to serve.
Toast the coriander and cumin lightly in a frying pan.
Add to all the remaining ingredients and blend until smooth.
Keep in a glass jar in the fridge for a few weeks.

t: Peri-peri prawns with onion disco fries
ing: 1 kg Woolworths easy to peel prawns
st: SautÃ© 1 finely chopped onion until translucent.
Add 2 cloves of garlic, 1 tbsp chopped chilli and 2 tsp chilli powder.
SautÃ© for a minute.
Add 2 tbsp tomato paste, 500 ml passata (purÃ©etomatoes)  and 2 tbsp sugar.
Simmer for 5 minutes.
Add 125 ml cream, season to taste then simmer for another 5 minutes.
In another pan melt 2 tbsp butter.
Toss in 1 kg Woolworths easy to peel prawns and stir-fry for 5 minutes.
Season with salt and pepper
Add the peri-peri sauce.
Simmer over high heat until prawns are cooked through.
Squeeze over some lemon juice, stir in the 2 tbsp chopped parsley then serve immediately with extra lemon wedges.
Mix together the almonds, parmesan, sage and seasoning.
Brush the pork chops with mustard, then coat with the nut mixture, pressing well to make sure the coating sticks.
Heat butter and oil in a pan, then cook the pork chops until golden on both sides, then place into the oven to finish cooking though.
Toss together the salad ingredients then serve with the hot pork chops.

ing: freshly ground black pepper, to taste
st: Place papaya, papaya seeds and pulp in a blender and puree till smooth.
Add the vinegar, honey, lemon juice, water, Dijon mustard, ginger, salt and pepper and blend.
Add the olive oil and blend again. Adjust seasoning with salt and pepper if necessary.

ing: 1/2 cup + 2 tbsp unsalted butter at room temperature
st: Split the papaya in half and scoop out the seeds. Save the 1 tablespoon of the seeds for the bread batter and reserve the rest for another use. Dice the papaya into Â½â chunks.

Place the papaya chunks, brown sugar, butter, lemon zest, and lemon juice in a pan. Cook on medium heat until the papaya chunks start to fall apart, about 8 to 10 minutes. Add vanilla extract. Remove from heat and puree. (Wait until it has cooled to use your blender.)
Preheat the oven to 350ËF and generously grease and flour a 9Ã5-inch loaf pan.
Place the flour, papaya seeds, baking soda, baking powder, cinnamon, nutmeg and salt in a medium bowl. Using a whisk, mix vigorously until uniform in color.

Place the butter and brown sugar in the bowl of a standing mixer fitted with the paddle attachment. Beat the butter until light and creamy, about two to three minutes on medium speed. Add the eggs one at a time, scraping down the sides with a spatula between additions. Add the yogurt and vanilla extract and beat to incorporate.

Add half the dry ingredients to the batter and beat until incorporated. Add the papaya puree and beat until incorporated. Add the remaining dry ingredients and beat until incorporated. Finally, fold in the shredded coconut and fresh ginger.

Scrape the batter into the prepared pan and bake for 60 to 70 minutes or until a toothpick or skewer placed in the center of the loaf comes out clean. Be sure to test several areas, as the toothpick may hit a wet papaya chunk area and look not done yet. You donât want to over bake the loaf.
Let cool in the pan for 15 minutes on a wire rack, before removing from pan to cool further. Top with shaved papaya ribbons before serving.
Combine and whisk all of the salad dressing ingredients (1/4 cup lime juice, 1/4 teaspoon salt, pinch of pepper and 1/2 cup olive oil) together.
Scoop the ripe papaya and 2 avocados out of the skins and discard the seeds.
Arrange over 80 g tender baby spinach leaves and spoon over dressing.
Season to taste and enjoy.

ing: sea salt and pepper to taste
1 1/2 cans coconut milk, plus 1/2 can water
1 sweet potato, peeled and chopped into cubes
2 tbsp Woolworths Thai red curry paste
2.5 cm fresh ginger root, peeled and sliced
1 red onion, cut into thin wedges
st: Pan fry the garlic, red onion, ginger, red curry paste and turmeric for 5 minutes until softened and fragrant.
Add the sweet potatoes, ripe papaya, coconut milk, fish sauce, red bell pepper and brown sugar to simmer for 40 minutes.
Serve warm with shredded rotisserie chicken, cubed fresh papaya, green chilli and coriander. Basmati rice or rotis are a delicious accompaniment to this curry.
Slice papaya in half lengthwise. Spoon out seeds and scrape away just enough meat to create a small well.
Fill each side with yoghurt, fruit and granola.
Drizzle with honey and sprinkle with a pinch of chia seeds or ground papayas seeds if desired.
Place the prawns, lime juice, salt, pepper and coriander into a bowl, then set aside for 5 minutes.
In another bowl, mix together the cucumber, radishes, red onion, chilli avocado and olive oil then season to taste.
Drain the liquid from the prawns, then toss with the other ingredients.
Separate the leaves of the baby gem lettuce, then spoon the ceviche.
Serve as a snack or starter.

ing: sea salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
1 x 400 g can chickpeas, drained and rinsed
sea salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
st: To make the soup, preheat the oven to 180Â°C. Season the parsnips and roast with 1 T olive oil for 25 minutes.
Fry the leeks, garlic and onion in the butter over a low heat for 5 minutes until soft. Add the roast parsnips, 2 T olive oil, chicken stock and thyme. Simmer for 40 minutes, or until tender.
Add the milk, season and blend until smooth. Just before serving, reheat the soup, fold in the sour cream and top with the spiced chickpeas.

To make the spiced chickpeas, preheat the oven to 200Â°C. Combine the chickpeas, cumin, paprika, lemon zest and seasoning. Toss with the olive oil and bake for 30 minutes, or until crunchy. Serve immediately sprinkled over the hot soup.

ing: 150 g baby spinach, blanched, drained and chopped
3/4 cup cake flour, plus extra for dusting
st: Place the eggs, onion, parmesan, flour, spinach and half the peas in a large bowl and mix to combine.
Add the ricotta and mix until just combined.
Roll heaped teaspoons of the mixture into balls and set aside on a lightly floured oven tray.
Melt the Bothamâs cremezola blue cheese and butter together in a saucepan over a low heat.
Pour in the cream and cook for about 3-4 minutes until the cream is thick. Season to taste.
Cook the gnocchi, in batches, in a large saucepan of salted boiling water for 3â4 minutes or until firm and floating to the surface.
Remove with a slotted spoon.
Place on an oven tray lined with non-stick baking paper and keep warm.
To serve place the gnocchi in a bowl then cover with the sauce.
Sprinkle with some parmesan and serve immediately.
In a deep jug, wide enough for your hand blender, add the egg, mustard, sugar, 1 clove of garlic, a pinch of pepper and the vinegar.
Blitz the lot together until the garlic is chopped up and incorporated (about 10 seconds).

Now add the sunflower oil, in a slow steady stream, blending the whole time. A cream coloured mayonnaise will start to form, you might find that you donât need all the oil. If unsure, stop, taste and decide. If it tastes very acidic, blend in more oil.
After blending, scoop into a sealable bottle and keep in the fridge for up to 1 week.

ing: maldon salt and pepper, to taste
st: Top and tail the Sugar Snap peas and the Mange Tout.
Pour some boiling water over the peas for a couple of minutes then drain
Place everything including the sliced red onions and crumbled feta into a salad bowl.
Make the vinaigrette: Add the oil, white wine vinegar, mustard and seasoning into a jar.
Shake jar to combine.
Drizzle over the salad to serve.

ing: 1 lemon, zested (if you're making lemon ricotta)
st: Open up cheese cloth and line colander with a double layer of the cloth, covering all the sides of the colander
Set over a deep bowl for draining
Pour milk into a heavy bottom sauce pan and set on medium to low heat
Let it heat slowly till it's about to boil
Add a 1/4 cup of lemon juice and almost immediately you will see curd form
Keep it on the heat and let the curd fully separate from the whey. The liquid should be clearish this won't take long just a minute or so
Take it off the heat
Using a slotted spoon, skim the curd out into the cheese cloth
Leave for 10 min to drain
Then gather ends of cheese cloth and tie it ti the sink handle to drain for another 10 minutes
Scoop out fresh ricotta into a storage container.
Use immediately or refrigerate for a couple of days.

ing: kiwi fruit, roughly sliced, to serve
st: Place the milk in the pot over a medium heat
Bring to a gentle simmer along with the vanilla, salt, sugar and creamed honey
Soak the gelatine sheets in cold water for 5 minutes or until soft
Add the softened gelatine to the mixture and stir until dissolved
Divide the mixture into 4-6 servings dishes/bowls depending on how many people your serving
Place in the fridge and set for 6 hours Or over night for best results
Drizzle some extra honey over and serve with the strawberries and kiwi fruit.

ing: icing pens or white icing in piping bag
st: Melt chocolate over a pot of simmering water. Be sure that the steaming water does not touch the bowl or the chocolate will seize (like a ghostâ¦well kind off)
Spray and cook the silicone cups, this just helps to ensure the chocolate cups remove easily from the cups, you wont have a problem but a back up is helpful.
Spoon melted chocolate into the cups and brush melted chocolate all up and around the sides of the cup. Place in the freezer to shock set it.
Lightly whip the peanut butter, this makes it easier to work with. And spoon into the set cups. Drizzle with more chocolate and smear it to the edges.
Place in the freezer again.
Line 4 baking trays, then draw 4x 18cm circles on the paper as templates.
Pulse the roasted nuts in a food processor until finely ground then stir in the corn flour.
In a large, clean bowl, whisk the egg whited until soft peaks form. Gradually add the sugar, a little at a time, while whisking until the mixture forms stiff glossy peaks.
Gently fold in then nut mixture.
Using a disposable piping bag, paint three stripes of red colour on the inside, then fill with the meringue mixture.
Pipe into the template in a spiral to make a round disk of meringue, repeat to make the four disks.
Bake for 1 hour, remove from the oven and leave to cool completely.
Bring the milk to the boil. In a bowl, whisk the egg yolks, caster sugar, vanilla and corn flour.
Pour the hot milk over the egg mixture, whisking continuously, then pour back into the pan.
Bring to the boil, stirring continuously then reduce the heat and simmer until smooth and thick. Remove from the heat and leave to cool completely in the fridge.
Once cool, stir in the strawberry puree and fold in the cream.
To assemble the dessert, place one of the meringue layers on a large, flat serving plate and spread with one-third of the strawberry custard filling and some chopped strawberries.
Place another meringue layer on top and spread with another third of the custard filling and strawberries, then repeat layering ending with a meringue layer.
Top with a pile of fresh strawberries and a drizzle of melted white chocolate.

ing: Woolworths sriracha flavoured nacho chips to top
Woolworths thin and crispy pizza bases
1 Woolworths rotisserie chicken, torn into large chunks
st: Coat the corn in the olive oil and season lightly  before roasting in the oven for 180 C for 15minutes or until slightly charred.
Coat the chucked chicken in BBQ marinade before adding to the pizza base.
Add charred corn, jalapeÃ±os and coriander.
Crumble the blue cheese over the pizza.
Place pizza in the oven to cook for 15-20minutes at 200 C.
Top with extra coriander, guacamole and nacho chips.
Preheat the oven to 180Â°C. Halve the lemons and remove most of the flesh from each half â leave a little flesh in the base of each âshellâ to prevent bitterness.
Stuff the lemon âshellsâ with the Parma ham slices and top with crumbled Gorgonzola. Grate over the Parmesan, then arrange on a baking tray and drizzle with olive oil.
Bake for 10 minutes or until bubbling and golden. Serve warm with glasses of bubbly.
To make the citrus bubbly, divide the freshly squeezed citrus juices between 4 Champagne glasses and top up with bubbly.

ing: salt and freshly ground black pepper
500 g Woolworths Conchiglie pasta, prepared as instructed
3 x 100 g Woolworths chargrilled marinated artichokes
st: Heat the 1/4 cup olive oil over a medium heat. Add the 3 x 100 g artichokes, 4 tbsp chopped basil,4 tbsp chopped parsley and 1 thinly sliced red chilli, cook together for a minute before adding the 450 g blanched prawns and toss together, cooking until warmed through.
Add it to a large mixing bowl before tossing with the chopped 95 g olives,  1 freshly squeezed lemon, 500 g  pasta and extra seasoning (salt and pepper) if needed.

To make the garlic crispy crumbs:Heat the 5 tbsp oil and 1 tbsp butter over a medium heat, add the 4 finely chopped garlic cloves, 1 finely chopped chilli and 6 basil leaves and cook for a few minutes until the mixture becomes fragrant. Add the 150 g breadcrumbs and toss through allowing the crumbs to toast further and become golden. Season with salt and freshly ground black pepper
Serve the crumb scattered over the pasta.

t: Maple syrup and blueberry glazed gammon
ing: Sea salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
4 kg Woolworths beech smoked traditional bogammonne in gammon
st: Preheat the oven to 180Â°C.

ing: Sea salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
st: Preheat the oven to 160Â°C. Rub the pork belly with 2 T olive oil and sprinkle with sea salt.
Arrange the carrots, onions and peppercorns in an ovenproof dish and top with the pork belly. Roast for 1Â½ hours, or until crisp and golden. Serve with the maple-roasted guavas.

To roast the guavas, arrange the fruit in a roasting pan and drizzle with 1 T olive oil, the maple syrup, brown sugar, seasoning and a few knobs of butter. Roast for 30 minutes until softened and slightly caramelised.

ing: 1.5 kg Easy to Cook Stuffed Pork Shoulder Roast Avg
st: Sign in/Register

ing: 50 g pecan nuts, toasted and roughly chopped
75 g cocoa powder, plus extra for rolling
st: Place the cream cheese, cocoa powder and xylitol in a mixing bowl. Using a silicon spatula or wooden spoon, mix the ingredients together until combined.
Roll into 10 equal sized truffles and roll in the extra cocoa, then roll in the nuts.
Make the ice cubes by placing the 1/2 cup of pomegranate seeds into an ice cube tray, cover with water, then freeze to form the ice cubes.
Place the peach puree, a splash of pomegranate juice and 1 tbsp rosemary leaves into tall glasses, then stir together.
Top with the ice cubes, then add the 1 L of sparkling water.
Garnish with sliced peach and a rosemary sprig.
Serve with a straw.
Drizzle a griddle pan with a little olive oil. Fry the courgettes on both sides until golden brown.
Remove and lightly toss with mint and lemon juice.
Season with salt and black pepper. Slice the halloumi cheese into strips and place on a warm fire.
Cook quickly, turning once, then serve with the courgettes.
Sign in/Register

ing: 1 French loaf, cut into thick slices
st: Heat 2 T of the olive oil with the red wine, garlic and chilli in a saucepan over a high heat.
Add the tomatoes and cook for 10 minutes until the sauce starts to thicken.

Meanwhile, heat the remaining 1 T olive oil in a large pan. Sear the steaks in the hot oil until well browned on both sides. This should take no more than 2 minutes on the first side, then no more than 4 on the other, depending on the thickness of the steak and how you like it done.
Transfer the steaks to a chopping board and leave to rest for a few minutes.
Toast the slices of French loaf in a hot pan (or under the grill or in a toaster) until golden, then spread with onion marmalade (optional).
Top with the steak and a generous spoonful of prego sauce.

ing: Sea salt and freshly ground black pepper
a small handful fresh mint, roughly chopped
8 thick slices Pain au levain pecan nut and raisin bread
st: Sign in/Register

Pour one punnet of the mixed berries and the punnet sobrosa strawberries, 1 cup of sugar, and the lemon juice into a medium sauce pan. Crush the berries lightly with a fork and bring the mixture to a full boil over medium-high heat. Lower the heat and simmer for 10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the mixture is syrupy. Fold the remaining berries into the hot mixture and refrigerate until very cold.

In the bowl of an electric mixer fitted with the whisk attachment, beat the cream, the remaining 3 tablespoons of sugar, and the vanilla together on medium-high speed until it forms firm peaks and set aside
Follow the instruction of the marshmallow frosting, whip and set aside
In decorative glassware layer a spoonful of the whipped cream, a spoonful of the berry compote, and then a few broken macaron pieces and lastly a spoon of the marshmallow frosting.
Repeat once or twice, depending on the size of the glasses, until the glasses are full, add a dollop of marshmallow frosting.
Brulee the frosting and garnish with fresh berries and mint.

ing: edible gold dust to coat berries
1/2 cup Woolworths fresh custard with vanilla bean seeds
st: Preheat oven to 130Â°C. Draw a circle with a 25cm diameter on silicone paper.

Use an electric mixer to whisk egg whites in a clean dry bowl until soft peaks form. Gradually add sugar, 1 tablespoon at a time, beating well after each addition, until meringue is thick and glossy and sugar dissolved. Rub a little meringue between fingers. If still "gritty" with sugar, continue to whisk until sugar dissolves. Add corn flour, vinegar and 1 tsp vanilla and whisk until just combined. Add the chopped mince pies and fold into the mixture.
Spoon meringue onto the silicone paper thatâs been placed on a tray, shaping a wreath leaving a hole in the center. Allow the mound of the mixture to be rough with jagged edges.

Place the tray with the wreath into the oven to slowly cook for 1 and a half hours, once done open the oven door slight and turn off the oven, allowing the Pavlova  wreath to cool. Before removing from the paper and placing on a serving dish.
For the custard cream: Whip the cream with the icing sugar and 1 tsp vanilla until thick before adding the custard and stirring through.
Add the raspberries and blackberries to a mixing bowl and add some gold edible dust before gently swirling the bowl to coat the berries in the gold dust.
Add the custard to the cooled wreath before gilding with the golden berries and finally top with the cherries.
Preheat the oven to 150Â°C.
Whisk the egg whites until frothy, then gradually add the sugar, whisking continually, until the mixture is thick, glossy and forms peaks.
Grease a sheet of baking paper, place on a baking tray and spread the meringue onto the paper in the shape of a pavlova.
Bake for 2Â½ hours, or until crunchy and cooked through but uncoloured.
Bring a large saucepan of water to the boil. Make small incisions into the underside of the peaches, then blanch in the water for 1 minute.
Plunge the blanched peaches into iced water. Peel, slice in half and remove the stones.
Heat the sugar, water, vanilla and rose syrup in a saucepan over a medium heat. Add the peaches and simmer for 5 minutes.
To serve, spoon the lemon cream over the cooled pavlova and top with the peaches.
To make the lemon cream, whip the cream until stiff. Mix the condensed milk and lemon juice, then gently fold into the whipped cream.
Score the skin of the duck, cut into chunks and marinate in the 1/4 cup of maple syrup and 1/2 cup of balsamic vinegar for 1 hour. Thread onto skewers.
Braai the skewers for 5 minutes on each side until crispy and cooked through.

To make the charred corn salad, parboil the 4 sweetcorn cobs, then braai until charred. Cut the corn off the cobs and toss with the remaining ingredients (20 g chopped coriander, 2 sliced peaches, 2 juiced limes and 2 tbsp red wine vinegar) until well combined.
Serve the maple duck skewers with the charred corn salad, wedges of lime and Parmesan.

ing: 1 pkt Woolworths Chocolate Brownie Mince Pies, broken up into small pieces
st: Grease a loaf pan with cooking spray and line with cling film â make sure there is enough overhanging to cover the dessert.
Stir the ice cream with a wooden spoon to soften then stir in the mince pies, spices and chocolate into the ice cream to ensure they are evenly distributed.
Spoon ice cream into the prepared pan and tap on work surface to remove any air bubbles, cover with cling film.
Freeze until set, about 4 hours or overnight
Unmould, the dessert and place onto a serving plate.
Top the dessert with roughly chopped WW chuckles

ing: sea salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
1x10 cm piece fresh ginger, thinly sliced
1 fennel bub, shaved and placed into iced water
st: Using a melon baller or ice cream scoop, scoop balls from the melons. To assemble, place the melon on a large serving platter. Pile the shaved fennel and pea shoots around the melon balls. Top with the ginger, drizzle with the salad dressing and squeeze over the orange.

ing: 4 Woolworths Ultimate sesame seed burger buns
st: Mix together the salsa ingredients in a bowl, season well, then set aside.
Make the guacamole, by mashing together the avo and lime, then season well and set aside.
Mix together the mayonnaise and sriracha.
Cook the burger patties until golden on both sides, then top with cheddar cheese and leave to melt.
Cut the burger buns in half, then toast lightly, before spreading both sides with the sriracha mayo.
Top with the salsa, then the burger patty and then finally a generous dollop of guacamole.

ing: 2 ripe mangoes, peeled and thinly sliced
st: Distribute the mango between four bowls, and top with the raspberries, coconut and a scattering of mint leaves.
Add a squeeze of lemon juice and lightly sprinkle with the crushed peppercorn. Serve immediately.

ing: 2 x 25 g blocks coconut ice, crushed
st: Beat the coconut milk until light and smooth, then add the vanilla seeds and beat further until combined. In a saucepan over a medium heat, poach the plums with the sugar and verjuice until soft.

PurÃ©e the plums and whisk into the coconut mixture before freezing. Once frozen, beat, then return to the freezer. When almost frozen, spoon the ice-cream mixture into a large yoghurt container and freeze again until completely set.

(Alternatively pour the mixture into an ice-cream machine and churn according to the manufacturerâs instructions.) Place the base of the container into hot water and carefully remove the ice cream from the container. Sprinkle liberally with coconut ice and top with thin slices of plum.

ing: 400 g ripe papaya, peeled and cut into blocks
st: Place the papaya pieces and lime juice in a blender and pulse until purÃ©ed. Set aside. In a saucepan, combine the caster sugar and 1 cup of water and bring to a gentle boil.

Cook for 15 minutes, or until syrupy. Fold the syrup into the purÃ©ed fruit, then pour the mixture into a freezer container and freeze until nearly set. Remove from the freezer and beat, then return to set fully.
Alternatively, churn in an icecream maker according to the manufacturerâs instructions. Slice into thick slabs and serve with wafer-thin pineapple slices.

ing: 1 pineapple, peeled and sliced into chunks
st: In a small saucepan, bring the water and sugar to a boil.
Turn down the heat and simmer until it starts to become syrupy.
Add the pineapple, reserving a few slices for serving, and simmer for 10 minutes. Remove from the heat and allow to cool.
Place in a blender and blend until smooth, then add the lemon juice and yoghurt and blend for a few seconds.
Add the mint and blend for a second or two. Pour into a container and place in the freezer.
Use a fork to break up the ice crystals when the mixture starts to freeze, then return to the freezer.
To make the caramelised lemon: Melt the sugar over a low heat in a large saucepan â do not stir.
When the sugar starts to melt, swirl the pot until it has all dissolved and starts to turn golden brown. Remove from the heat and cool slightly â be careful not to burn your fingers.
Dry the lemon pieces with a paper towel and dip into the caramel. Serve with the sorbet and slices of fresh pineapple.
In a large bowl, mix together the popcorn, nuts, sesame seeds, cranberries and cocoa nibs.
In a saucepan, mix together the honey and the coconut oil then heat gently until simmering.
Remove from the heat, then pour over the popcorn mixture, toss well, then transfer to a lined square baking tin. Press mixture down firmly to make sure it sticks together.
Leave to cool completely before breaking or slicing into portions.

ing: 3 tbsp butter, and an extra 2 tablespoon for dotting
2 sheets woolworths all butter puff pastry
st: Halve the nectarines and remove the stones. Heat the sugar and butter together over a medium heat along with Â½ cup of water.

Allow the mixture to melt together before adding the nectarines, cut side town. Let the water reduce before almost gone then add the extra butter, dotting it over the nectarines. Cover with the sheets of pastry before placing in the oven to bake for 20-25 minutes at 180.
Once golden and puffed, remove from the oven and cover with a plate. Carefully turn the plate over to reveal the cooked nectarines.
Serve with scoops of the mascarpone vanilla cream.
Preheat oven to 200C
Place sugar and water into a pan, then stir until sugar dissolves.
Simmer until the mixture bubbles and caramelizes to a light caramel.
Remove from the heat, then add the port, vanilla and butter, then swirl until the mixture is smooth â remove from the heat.
Carefully arrange the plums onto the caramel, alternating cut side down, then round-side down.
Roll the pastry out into a large round, then place the pastry over the plums. Tuck the pastry around the edges of the fruit.
Bake the tart in the preheated oven for 20 minutes, or until the pastry is golden and crisp.
Once cooked, leave to stand for one minute, then turn tart out of the pan â it must be turned out while still warm otherwise the caramel will set and the tart will be stuck to the pan.
Serve with vanilla ice cream.
Place the orange zest, juice, honey and water into a pot, then bring to the boil.
Add the nectarines, then simmer gently, with a lid on for 15 minutes or until the fruit is tender.
Remove the fruit from the pot, then simmer the liquid until reduced by half before pouring over the fruit and setting aside to cool.
Place the vanilla pod and milk into a pot, then bring to a simmer.
Whisk together the egg yolks, cornflour and sugar.
Pour the hot milk onto the eggs, while whisking.
Return the mixture to the pot, then stir with a wooden spoon over gentle heat until mixture thickens and coats the back of a spoon.
Pour through a sieve then chill or serve immediately.
Serve the poached fruit drizzled with a generous helping of custard, and a sprinkling of crushed biscuits.
Steam the pears in a steamer until they start to soften. Using a sharp knife, slice through carefully.
Sprinkle with some of the oats and seeds then plate.
Serve the yoghurt and remaining oats and seeds on the side. Drizzle with the honey.
Cream butter and sugar together
Add the egg, beating well to combine
Add the cake flour, baking powder and salt
Mix thoroughly to form a stiff dough
Press the dough evenly into a tart tin
Dock the pastry base
Blind bake at 180Â°C for 30 min or until the pastry is golden and crispy

t: Paprika and butter bean stuffed tomatoes
ing: 1 x 400 g butter beans can, drained
sea salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
st: Sign in/Register
Mix the flour, water, yeast and salt. Fold in the baby spinach and cauliflower.
Heat the oil over a medium to high heat. Using a tablespoon, spoon the batter into the oil and fry in batches until golden brown and cooked through. Drain on kitchen paper and season with salt.

ing: cultured cream creme fraiche, for serving
st: Brown the chicken mince in canola oil. Add the smoked paprika, chilli sauce and can of red kidney beans. Simmer until cooked through.
Heat the tortillas in a dry pan until browned on both sides. Serve with a spoonful of the mince, top with fresh coriander, a dollop of crÃ¨me fraÃ®che and chopped chilli, if you like.

ing: 2 x 250 g tubs plain full-cream cream cheese
100 g blueberries, plus extra to garnish
st: Grease a round 24 cm loose-bottomed tart tin with a little oil.
Place the biscuits in a food processor and blitz until fine, or crush in a bag. Transfer to a bowl and mix in the butter.
Press the biscuit mixture firmly into the greased tart tin, and up the sides. Chill for 20 minutes.
To make the filling, beat the cream cheese until smooth and gradually add the condensed milk. Mix until well incorporated. Fold in the lemon zest.
Spoon the filling evenly into the tart tin. Chill for 1 hour.
Place the blueberries, lemon juice and sugar in a saucepan over a medium to high heat and cook for 5 minutes, or until soft and juicy.
When ready to serve, remove the cheesecake from the fridge and gently push the out of the tin. Garnish with the glazed blueberries, berries and plums.

ing: cultured cream creme fraiche, for serving
st: Brown the chicken mince in canola oil. Add the smoked paprika, chilli sauce and can of red kidney beans. Simmer until cooked through.
Heat the tortillas in a dry pan until browned on both sides. Serve with a spoonful of the mince, top with fresh coriander, a dollop of crÃ¨me fraÃ®che and chopped chilli, if you like.

t: Pepper steak pie with herbed potatoes
ing: 700 g garlic & herb potatoes, prepared as instructed
st: Cook the pie in the oven according to the packet instructions.
Cut the potato packet corner, then cook the potatoes in the microwave until tender (about 7 minutes â check packet instructions).
Place the cooked potatoes into a bowl, then crush with a fork. Stir in the cream cheese, basil, parsley and seasoning.
Heat the olive oil in a pot, then add the onions, a pinch of salt and the sugar then cook on medium heat until the onions have softened and are browning.
Add the flour and stir and cook for 1 minute.
Stir in the stock, then leave to simmer for 5 minutes until sauce is thickened, then season to taste.
Serve a slice of pie, along with the potatoes and a few spoonfuls of gravy

t: Pear, coconut and vanilla rocky road
ing: 150 g Dried pear, coconut and vanilla cookies
100 g mini pink and white marshmallows
st: Place chocolate, butter and syrup into a glass bowl then heat gently over bain marie until melted.
In a large bowl, roughly crumble in the cookies then mix in the coconut, marshmallows, nuts and dried pears.
Pour in the melted chocolate then stir thoroughly until everything is well mixed.
Press into a lined square baking dish.
Place into the fridge to set for 20 minutes.
Remove from the tin, cut into 16 even squares!

t: Pulled beef, roast veg mac and cheese
ing: Woolworths Easy to Cook pulled beef shin
st: Preheat oven to 200C.
Place the vegetables into a roasting dish, then drizzle with oil, add thyme and season. Roast for 20 minutes or until the vegetables are tender.
Place the butter for the white sauce and melt over a medium heat.
When the butter is melted, mix the flour in to make a smooth paste.  Cook it for 1 minute.  Take off the heat.
Mix in the milk, a little bit at a time, to make sure there are no lumps.
Put the pot back on the stove and heat it up to boiling.  Stir it all the time.  Let it boil for 5 minutes and take it off the heat.  Add the salt, pepper and mustard.  Stir in half the cheese.
Cook the beef shin according to the packet instructions.
Mix together the white sauce, beef, vegetables and macaroni, then transfer to an oven dish.
Scatter the remaining cheese on the top then bake for 20 minutes until the cheese is melted and browning on top.

ing: 300 g linguini pasta, boiled till al dente
st: Heat oil in a pan then sautÃ© spring onions until tender.
Add chilli, garlic and prawns, then saute until prawns are browned.
Add cream, peas and season then leave to simmer gently for 2 minutes.
Toss in the pasta, lemon zest, juice and parsley.
Serve immediately.

ing: 2 x 150 g double cream coconut lime yoghurt
st: Combine the pineapple, yoghurt, ice, chia seeds, oats and pineapple in a blender, then blend until smooth.
Pour into bowls, then garnish before serving.

ing: Woolworths butterflied Moroccan chicken, prepared as instructed
1 large sweet potato, cut into thin wedges
salt and freshly ground pepper, to taste
extra virgin olive oil, to drizzle over and coat
st: In the same oven that the chicken is roasting in: Add the veggies to a roasting tray and season with the salt and pepper before tossing with the olive oil to coat then place in the oven to roast for about 35 minutes or until charred on the outside and tender inside.
Serve the Moroccan chicken with the vegetables with the dressing drizzled over and lemon wedges on the side

ing: 3 cm fresh ginger, peeled and roughly chopped
extra virgin olive oil, for drizzling
st: For the paste: Dry-roast all the spices for 5 - 8 mins over medium heat to release fragrant oils. Grind until fine. Using a blender or food processor, combine wet and dry ingredients and blend to make the paste.
Rub meat generously with paste (keep 125 ml paste for the sauce). Marinate meat for 2 days in a sealed plastic zip lock bag in the refrigerator.
Preheat oven to 160 Â°C.
Sear the marinated roast in a pan with butter until golden brown on all sides. Remove and place on baking tray.
Drizzle with olive oil and place in oven.
To cook a perfect roast, use a meat thermometer.Rare: 120 Â°C â 130 Â°CMedium: 135 Â°C â 145 Â°CMedium well: 145 Â°C â 155 Â°C
Remove from oven and cover with foil.
Rest meat for 15 â 20 mins before carving.
Keep the pan juices to use
Mix remaining paste with pan juices and place pot on the stove.
Add coconut milk and cook till sauce thickens.
Strain and pour sauce into blender with 10 g of the fresh coriander. Blend and heat before serving.
Serve the sauce and pomegranate on the side and garnish with fresh coriander.

For the pap: Bring the water to the boil along with the salt. Add the flour and begin stirring gently. Once all combined begin stirring a little faster over a slightly lower heat. Continue stirring for 5-7 minutes before tasting if extra seasoning is needed.

For the chakalaka: Heat the oil over a medium heat before adding the onions and slowly cooking until caramelized. Add the garlic and spices and begin stirring together in the pot to toast the spices and combine the ingredients.
After about 1 minute of cooking add the carrots, cabbage and peppers. At this stage the pot might seem dry, just add some oil.
Once the veggies have softened add the beans, vinegar and season with salt and freshly ground black pepper.
Prepare the sausage by adding the oil to a pan and heating over a medium heat. Add the sausage and begin cooking slowly, until it begins to brown slightly, about 5 minutes.
Turn over and cook the other side in the same manner, serve  the sausage with the pap, chakalaka and gravy prepared as instructed.

ing: oil or sunflower oil, for frying
st: Mix together the flour, baking powder, bicarb and salt.
Whisk together egg and buttermilk then mix enough into the dry ingredients to form a thick batter.
Fold in the pickled fish and 4 Tbsp of coriander.
Heat oil then drop spoonfulls of mixture into the oil and fry until browned.
Drain on kitchen paper to remove excess oil.
For the dipping sauce, mix together the mayonnaise, chutney and the last 2 Tbsp of coriander and serve alongside the hushpuppies.
Pre-heat oven to 230Â°C or highest setting
Slice skin side of pork belly into diamonds, being careful not to score to deep.
Rub the meat side of the pork with the marinade (not the skin)
Pat dry the pork skin with paper towel until completely dry and rub with coarse salt powder getting into the diamonds.
Place in a large ovenproof dish and into oven for 30-35min until crackling is golden brown.
Remove from oven and drop the temp to 150Â°C
Place the carrots, onion, celery, garlic & apple under the pork belly.
Add the verjuice and place back into the oven for 2-3 hours until very soft & tender.
Put the grill on for the last 5 min if you would like extra crispy crackling.
Place the apples, sugar, and butter into a pan, then cook until the apples begin to caramelize, then add the pecan nuts and set aside.
Boil the dated in the water for 5 minutes to soften, then stir in the bicarb and set aside to cool.
Grease a 2L oven dish, then preheat the oven to 180C.
Cream the butter, muscovado sugar and vanilla together until light and fluffy.
Mix in the eggs, one at a time until mixed in well.
Add the molasses, then fold in the flour and milk.
Stir in the softened dates and caramelized apples, then transfer the mixture into the oven dish.
Bake for about 40-45 minutes until risen and firm to the touch.
Place all the sauce ingredients into a pot and heat gently while stirring until melted, bring to the boil and simmer until thickened â about 5 minutes.
Once baked, remove the pudding from the oven and pour the sauce over.
Serve with custard.
For the chicken livers: Heat the butter and oil in a pan over a medium heat.  Add the onions, peppers and garlic before cooking slowly until softened and lightly caramelized.

Add the chicken livers and cover with a lid. Cook for 2 minutes before turning the livers over and cooking for another 2-3 minutes. Add the peri peri sauce. Cook for another minute then turn off the heat.

For the spicy spinach: Heat the butter and oil over a medium heat before adding the garlic and spring onion. Cook for a minute before adding the spinach and wilting down with the cream. Cook for a few minutes to reduce before adding the tomato chutney. Season with salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste.

For the grilled corn: Heat the butter and oil together before adding the garlic and peppers. Caramelise before adding the corn and increasing the heat to high. Cook until lightly charred. Finish with the chilli and Parmesan and toss through the corn before finishing with some seasoning.

t: Picanha roast with mash and salad
st: Preheat the oven to 220Â°C. Coat the beef in the olive oil, rosemary, mustard, salt and freshly ground black pepper, rubbing it all over to ensure the flavours penetrate well.

Add the meat to a roasting dish and place in the oven to roast for 30 minutes or a little longer if you prefer it done a little more. Remove the meat from the oven and allow it to rest for 10 minutes before slicing and serving.

For the mash: Add the butternut to water that has been seasoned with salt, pepper, garlic, butter and thyme. Bring to the boil and cook the butternut until just tender before draining and mashing with the remaining butter and extra seasoning.

Heat a griddle pan over a medium heat: Coat the beans and marrow in some olive oil before adding to the griddle pan, ensure the marrow goes down cut side down first. Allow them to brown before turning over. Continue cooking and turning over until tender.
In a large serving bowl add the spinach and the dressing, add the marrow and beans and toss together.
Serve the roast with the mash and green veg salad.

Place baking or silicone paper down on a baking tray, spread the chocolate over then roll the paper up creating a tube of paper with chocolate in between, divined the melted chocolate in half so you can make 2 rolls of the melted chocolate.
Place the rolls of melted chocolate in the fridge to set until firm.
Prepare the vanilla bean icing as per the instructions using the butter and milk. Attach a flower petal nozzle to a piping bag before adding the icing.

Place the cake on a icing turn table before laying the nozzle horizontally at the base of the cake. Begin gently squeezing while turning the cake turn table to create a frill at the bottom of the cake. Once youâve gone around the whole round of the cake donât stop simply begin creating another layer, donât worry if it looks a little uneven of off set, the weight of the icing will cause the layers to fall in place. Continue icing in this manner until the sides are completely covered making the cake look like itâs wearing a frilly skirt.

Remove the chocolate roll from the fridge and carefully unroll breaking the chocolate into white chocolate bark. Place the bark on top of the cake before arranging the chocolates, biscuits and soet koekies.

t: Pulled pork and beetroot slaw tacos
st: Cook the pork in the oven according to the packet instructions.
In a large bowl, toss together the beetroot, carrots, onion, cabbage, sesame seeds and coriander seeds.
Mix together the vinegar, lime juice, sugar, salt and pepper, then pour over the coleslaw and toss well to dress.
Place some salad into the taco shell, then top with the pulled pork.
Garnish with more fresh coriander to serve.

ing: 400 g pork rashers, each rasher sliced into 3
1 Tbsp Lazy Kettle Hickory Liquid Smoke
1 ciabatta, sliced and lightly toasted to serve
st: Heat a saucepan over medium to high heat, with a little oil. Fry the pork rashers until golden and the fat has rendered out. Remove the pork.

Add the chopped leeks to the pork fat and fry until golden.  Add the garlic, smoked paprika, chilli flakes and continue cooking for a few seconds. Add the rest of the ingredients, along with the pork rashers and simmer for 10-15 minutes.
Season with salt and serve with slices of toasted ciabatta.

ing: 4 Tbsp tomato paste with vegetable soffritto
st: Combine all the ingredients for the meatballs, except the oil, in a bowl. Roll into balls and fry in a nonstick pan over a medium to high heat until golden. Finish off in the oven at 180Â° C to cook through.
To make the tomato sauce, fry the leeks in a little olive oil until soft. Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute. Add the remaining ingredients and simmer for 20 minutes.
Serve with Woolworths fresh tagliatelle, cooked al dente.
WINE:Renzo Masi Chianti

ing: Sea salt and freshly ground black pepper
st: Heat the oil over a medium heat before adding the mushrooms and letting them simmer and brown without being disturbed for about 1-2 minutes.
Toss the pan gently and cook for another minute before adding the walnuts, garlic, butter, rosemary and season. Cook for about 5 minutes or until fragrant and the garlic has cooked.
Add the cream and reduce the heat to low. Crumble in the blue cheese and allow to melt through, season with extra black pepper.
Cook the gnocchi as per the instructions.
Heat the butter over a medium heat. Once the gnocchi is cooked add it to the melted butter and cook for about 2 minutes a side or until crisp and golden.
Add the gnocchi to a serving dish and top with the mushroom sauce before serving.

ing: 2 x 250 g plain cream cheese tubs, at room temperature
st: Preheat the oven to 160Â°C. Grease and line 1 x 22 cm springform cake tin.
Whisk the egg whites until stiff and gradually add the sugar, beating well between each addition. Once all the sugar has been incorporated, add the lemon zest.
Mix the baking powder with the ground almonds and fold half into the meringue, along with half the olive oil. When fully incorporated, add the remaining ground almonds and olive oil.
Half-fill the cake tin and bake for 20 minutes, or until a skewer comes out clean. Repeat with the remaining cake batter.
To make the cream cheese icing, place the cream cheese in a bowl and soften with a wooden spoon. Once smooth, stir through the maple syrup and vanilla seeds.

To make the caramel corn flake crown, line a baking tray with greaseproof paper or a silicone baking mat. Spread the cornflakes onto the tray. Place the sugar in a heavy-bottomed saucepan over a low heat and stir until the sugar has dissolved. Once the sugar has dissolved, stop stirring and increase the heat. Allow to boil until the syrup has caramelised and turned golden. Remove from the heat and pour over the cornflakes. Set aside until the syrup has set and the cornflakes can be broken into large shards.

To assemble the cake, sandwich the layers together with the cream cheese icing. Use the remaining icing to decorate the top and sides of the cake. Top with the caramel cornflake crown and chocolate shards. Roll out the marzipan, cut out stars using a cookie cutter and decorate the cake.Cookâs note: The cake batter can be left to stand and baked at a later stage.
Spoon the coconut yoghurt into four shallow bowls.
Swirl a teaspoon of peanut butter into each bowl.
Top with a generous sprinkle of muesli.
Add a few sliced strawberries, and drizzle with honey to serve.

ing: 400 g Italian diced tomato with herbs
400 g Three bean mix in brine
st: Break or cut your meatballs into bite-sized chunks, we like to quarter them.
Cut the sweetcorn off the cob and set aside
Heat up your pan on high, then add 1 tablespoon of olive oil
Add your meatballs to the pan and sizzle for 5 minutes, then remove from the heat
Add the sweetcorn to the pan and cook for 2 minutes, or until it starts to blacken
Put the meatballs back into the pan with the sweetcorn
Add the canned tomato and drained beans, and cook for 5 minutes
Add your cooked rice to the mixture, then stir and cook for a further 2 minutes or until heated through.
A small coffee plunger
A moka pot
Access to a stove

ing: 7 cardamom pods, crushed and husks removed
st: preheat the oven to 180Â°C. Mix the coconut, egg whites, sugar and grapefruit zest in a bowl. Use to line a 27 cm x 5 cm deep pie dish. Bake for 3 to 5 minutes until crisp and set. Reduce the ovenâs temperature to 160Â°C.
To make the filling, bring the milk to a boil in a saucepan over a medium heat. In a mixing bowl, whisk the egg yolks and sugar until creamy. Add the flour, cornflour and salt and mix.

Slowly add the warm milk while whisking, taking care not to add too much at a time as this could scramble the eggs. Once all the milk is incorporated, pour the mixture back into the saucepan and return to the heat.

Cook, stirring continually, until the mixture thickens. Once the filling coats the back of the spoon, remove from the heat and add the butter, vanilla seeds, cardamom and naartjie zest. Stir until the butter has melted and is incorporated into the filling.
Beat the egg whites until stiff peaks form, then gently fold into the batter. Spoon the batter into the coconut crust and bake for 20 minutes. Serve with the candied citrus peel.
Preheat the oven to 180Â°C.
Heat the sunflower oil over a medium heat. Roughly chop the onion and sautÃ© in a pan with the cumin, smoked paprika and garlic.
Add the pork mince and brown. Add the tomatoes and drained corn. Season to taste and cook for a further 5 minutes.
Roll out the shortcrust pastry to a thickness of 2.5 to 3 mm.
Using a saucer, cut out rounds of the pastry and spoon the pork mixture into the centre of each round.
Fold over and crimp the edges with a fork.
Brush with egg and bake for 15 minutes, or until golden.
Prepare the couscous according to package instructions.
Cut the olives in half. Take half of the tomatoes and cut them in half. Take half of the basil and chop finely.
Fry the chicken in a pan on high heat with 20 ml oil for 5 minutes.
Add the olives, whole and halved tomatoes and cook for another
10 minutes. Remove from heat and add chopped basil (if using).
Plate the couscous and top with the chicken. Garnish with olive oil and the remaining basil leaves.

t: Mac n cheese with crisp bacon
ing: 60 g dry breadcrumbs, very finely ground
st: Preheat the oven to 220Â°C.
Grill the bacon until crisp. Mix with the breadcrumbs and Parmesan.
Drizzle the tomatoes with balsamic and olive oil and roast for 10 minutes or until soft.
In a saucepan, melt the butter and add the flour, stirring continuously, to form a paste.

Cook for 1 minute, then remove from the heat and gradually add the milk and cream, whisking continuously. Return to the heat and simmer for 5 minutes, stirring. Add the Emmenthal and nutmeg and season.

Arrange the rigatoni standing upright in a greased baking dish. Ladle the sauce into the pasta tubes, ensuring all the pasta is covered. Arrange the roast tomatoes on top and sprinkle with the cheesy bacon crumbs.
Bake for 20 minutes, or until golden brown.

ing: Woolworths Madagascan vanilla ice cream, for serving
st: Preheat the oven to 180Â°C. Cut the crusts off the bread.
Mix the eggs and cream using a whisk.
Spread 4 slices of bread with Nutella and the remaining 4 with peanut butter. Sandwich the Nutella slices with a peanut butter slice.

In a large pan, heat the oil and butter until the butter is foamy, then dip each sandwich into the egg mixture and pan-fry on both sides until golden brown. Finish off in the oven to make sure they are piping hot.
Serve for breakfast or dessert, with cinnamon sugar or ice cream.
Sign in/Register

ing: 3 slabs Nestle Peppermint Crisp, roughly broken into chunks
st: Whip the cream until soft peaks form. (I use an electric stand-mixer for about 3 minutes on a medium speed and then speed it up for the last minute.) In a separate bowl, beat the caramel with a fork to loosen and to ensure a smooth texture.
Gently fold the caramel into the whipped cream, then add most of the chocolate pieces (set aside a cupful for decoration).

Line a 30 x 22 x 6.5 cm dish with a single layer of whole Tennis biscuits. Top with half the caramel mixture, then add another layer of Tennis biscuits. Pour the remainder of the caramel mixture over the second layer of Tennis biscuits.
Sprinkle the last of the Peppermint Crisp chunks over the top. Cover with tin foil and chill for at least 7 hours before serving.
Combine all the ingredients except the salt, ice and basil. Allow to stand for 2 hours, then pour into glasses rimmed with pink salt and filled with ice. Garnish with basil leaves.
âAn alternative way of removing the arils is to open the pomegranate and submerge it in a bowl of water. The rubies will fall to the bottom while the membranes float to the top.â

ing: 500 g Extra Large Black Tiger Prawns
st: Stir-fry 500 g Woolworths extra-large black tiger prawns in 1 tsp ghee and 1 x 50 g sachet Woolworths vindaloo Indian curry paste.
In a separate pan, heat 2 tsp ghee over a medium heat.
Add 1 tsp grated fresh turmeric, 1 tsp crushed garlic, 1 tsp grated ginger, 1 tsp crushed chilli, 2 tsp Woolworths breyani spice and a pinch of saffron.
Fry until fragrant. Cook Woolworths basmati rice according to package instructions and serve with the prawns.
Preheat the oven to 120Â°C. Beat 4 free-range egg whites with a pinch of salt until foamy.
Gradually add 200 g caster sugar and beat until the mixture is glossy and soft peaks form.
Spoon the mixture into small circles onto a baking tray lined with greaseproof paper and bake for 2â3 hours, or until crispy.
Mix 1 x 360 g can Nestle peppermint Caramel Treat with Â½ cup whipped cream.
Sandwich the meringues together using the caramel mixture.

ing: 1/2  cup coriander, roughly chopped (reserve some for serving)
st: Preheat the oven to 200Â°C. Rub the whole chicken with the chicken masala and olive oil. Roast the chicken for 30â45 minutes, or until the skin is golden brown and crisp, turning once. Set aside.

Heat the butter in a large saucepan. Gently fry the onion, green pepper, garlic, celery and ginger. Add the spices and buckwheat and fry for a further 3â5 minutes, or until the onion is translucent and lightly caramelised.
Stir in the chicken stock and cook over a medium-high heat until the buckwheat is cooked.
Add the roast chicken (either whole or shredded) and the tomato paste, honey and salt and stir gently. Simmer for 10 minutes, then stir in half the coriander.
Mix the labneh, turmeric and lime zest. Dollop onto the soup and garnish with the remaining coriander.

ing: 1 tbsp Mediterranean Extra Virgin Olive Oil
st: 1 T ground cumin
1 T smoked paprika
3 garlic cloves, crushed
1 t dried oregano
1â2 t salt
A few twists black pepper
1 T olive oil
2 T lime juice

ing: 2 citrus, peeled and cut into segments
st: Preheat the oven to 200Â°C.
Mix the blueberries, muesli and honey together, until sticky and firm. Spoon the mixture into muffin cups and press down to form a crust.
Bake in the oven for 20 minutes. Remove and cool. Remove the muesli crusts from the muffin cups and allow to cool further.
Top with the sliced papaya and orange segments. Squeeze over the lime juice.
Liquidise the mint leaves and plain yoghurt and drizzle the mixture over the tartlets.

ing: 1 sheet nori, cut into thin strips
st: Wash the cabbage and slice finely. Place the cabbage in a sieve with the carrot and squeeze out as much moisture as possible. Place in a bowl and toss with the remaining kimchi ingredients. Transfer to a jar and chill.

Roll the sausage meat into balls. Heat the olive oil in a pan. Fry the meatballs until golden brown. Add the ginger and paprika and shake the pan to coat the meatballs. Add the honey and shake to coat the meatballs again. Set aside until ready to use.

To assemble, liberally spread the pomodoro sauce onto a precooked pizza base, place the meatballs on top, then add spoonfuls of kimchi. Preheat the oven to 200Â°C and bake the pizza until the edges are slightly charred. Top with the nori and microherbs.

ing: 12 tbsp ginger preserve or marmalade (or 6tbsp of each)
3 tbsp dark rum or Grand Marnier (optional)
st: Sign in/Register
Preheat the oven to 120Â°C. Whisk the butter and sugar together until light and creamy.
Add the orange zest and egg yolks and combine well.
Slowly add the warm milk while whisking.
Whisk the egg whites until stiff peaks form, then fold into the mixture.

Divide the mixture between six ramekins or small bowls (you can grease them with cooking spray). Place the ramekins in a large baking dish, then fill with water until it comes halfway up the sides of the ramekins. Bake for 40 minutes. Remove from the oven but leave the custards in the water to cool slightly.
For a decadent dessert, serve with dark chocolate ganache and chocolate shavings. Or garnish with sliced seasonal fruit for a lighter approach.
A crisp caramel topping, as for crÃ¨me brÃ»lÃ©e, is another option.

t: Pita bread with falafel and sour cream
st: Add chickpeas, chickpea brine, flour and falafel spice to a food processor. Pulse until the mixture resembles a coarse mix with a mealy meally texture. Be careful not to over blend.
Scoop a teaspoon (15g) of the mixture at a time and roll into balls. Wet your hands before you form the balls.
Deep fry the falafel balls in vegetable oil.
Serve with warm pita bread, falafel and sour cream.

ing: No added salt & sugar peanut butter
st: Toast the bread until golden brown and butter while still warm

Heat a little butter and honey in a pan until foaming.  Slice the banana length ways and sautÃ© in the pan for a few seconds until caramelised.  Remove and add the strawberries and swirl around until slightly soft.

Spread the buttered toast with peanut butter. Top one slice with the caramelized banana and spread the other with strawberry jam and top with the strawberries. Drizzle with extra honey to taste. Serve with milk.
To prepare the pizza, fry the boerewors balls in olive oil until caramelized.
Spread 4 T chakalaka onto the base, top with boerewors and mozzarella .
Bake at 180°C for 15-20 minutes.
Season with salt and pepper, top with basil.
Optional: Serve with roasted butternut and beetroot salad.
Secret ingredient: Chakalaka, use as pizza base topping
Season chicken, the heat olive oil in a pan over medium heat.
Cook the chicken for 5 minutes on each side then add in the butter and sage and cook for a 3 minutes continuously basting the chicken with the butter.
Once the butter had turned golden brown, add the lemon juice and cook for a further minute.
Serve with Roasted baby potatoes with garlic herb butter.

ing: sweet and sticky pork loin ribs
200 g freshly smashed spicy jalapeno avo
1 pineapples, sliced into quarters down the middle
180 g Sheep and goats milk feta
st: Prepare the ribs as per packaging instructions.

While those are on the braai, prepare the grilled mozzarella toasties by cutting the garlic bread all the way through, spread mayonnaise on the outside of each piece of bread, spread the atchar on the inside and top with mozzarella.
Season and put the toasties in a braai grid and cook until melty and caramelized.
Cut the avocados in half, grill on the braai and fill with spicy guacamole.
Grill the pineapples on the braai and finish off with lime juice.
Combine the dressing ingredients and toss through the greens, top with feta and seasoning.

t: Nectarine snacking cake - a total treat
ing: 150 g sugar, plus 2 T for dusting
Â¼ cup sour cream or yoghurt
st: Line an 18 x 9cm cake tin with baking paper or grease with butter and a light dusting of sugar.â¯Preheat the oven to 200ÂºC.
In a mixing bowl, cream the butter and sugar together until light and fluffy.â¯Add one egg at a time and whisk untilâ¯well incorporated. Repeat with the other egg.
Fold the dry ingredients into the egg mixture and add the sour cream and orange zest. Pour the batter into the prepared tin.
Layer the slicednectarineson top, sprinkle with the almonds and an extra dusting of sugar.â¯Bake for 15â20 minutes, or until cooked through.
Serve with a dollop of yoghurt, toasted almond flakes and a drizzle of honey.

ing: Sea salt flakes, a generous pinch
60 g Sea Salt and Pepper Croutons
st: To make the dressing, use the back of a knife or a pestle and mortar and crush the garlic and sea salt together to make a paste. Add the Dijon mustard and stir together to combine.

Slowly add the olive oil in a steady stream while stirring to emulsify, adding a squeeze of lemon to taste. It should be lovely and thick â but add a few tablespoons of water to loosen the dressing if you like. Alternatively, add all the dressing ingredients to a jar and shake well until emulsified.
Drizzle over ripe avo, crisp lettuce and radishes. Top with croutons and grated Parmesan and eat immediately. Great with steak or Sunday lunch roast chicken.

ing: 1 cup Woolworths Double Cream Strawberry Yoghurt
st: Blend the melon, lemon juice and sugar syrup.
Pour into the lolly moulds until filled halfway and freeze until solid. Top with a layer of strawberry yoghurt, insert the lolly sticks and freeze again.
Unmould the frozen lollies, sprinkle with dehydrated strawberries and enjoy!

Pour 1 can of WoolworthsOrganic RosÃ©into two chilled glasses. Top with Woolworths Rose-flavoured Sparkling Water. Add frozen raspberries (and ice if you want), garnish with fresh mint or micro mint leaves and enjoy!

ing: 200 g skinless chicken breast fillets, cut into small cubes
100 g fresh baby corn, sliced into roundels
1 lime or lemon, sliced in half
st: 2 free range eggs
200 g Skinless chicken breast fillets, cut into small cubes
100 g Fresh baby corn, sliced into roundels
Handful of fresh parsley, chopped
1 Lime or lemon, sliced in half

ing: 375 g Woolworths Full Fat Cream Cheese
Woolworths Homestyle Oat Snaps, to serve
st: Strawberry cheesecake: Simmer 200 g sliced strawberries with the juice of a lemon, 2 T castor sugar and splash of water for a few minutes until sticky and syrupy. Allow allow to cool completely before folding through the cheesecake frosting. Sandwich between Woolworths Homestyle Oat Snaps.
Chocolate cheesecake cookies: Stir a teaspoon of cocoa powder through the sweetened and whipped cream cheese and sandwich between Woolworths Chocolate Digestive Biscuits.
Lemon cheesecake cookies: Stir a spoon or two of Woolworths Lemon Curd through the whipped cream cheese and sandwich between Woolworths Ginger Biscuits. Enjoy!

ing: CrÃ¨me fraiche or sour cream to serve
6 â 8 Woolworths Apache Potatoes, rinsed and thinly sliced
st: Preheat the oven to 200Â°C
Toss the sliced potatoes in 2 T olive oil, garlic butter, rosemary and seasoning.
Roast for 30 minutes or until lightly golden and crunchy. (These also make the ultimate bar snack)
Set aside while you make your pizza.

ing: 2â3 Flavourburstâ¢ Envyâ¢ apples, halved and cored
1 x 250 g Woolworths Frozen All Butter Puff Pastry, thawed
st: Preheat the oven to 180CÂ°.

Slice your Envyâ¢ apples super thinly and place in the bowl with lemon juice, cinnamon and sugar and microwave for 3 minutes until softened and the slices are evenly coated. This helps the apples bend without breaking.
Roll your sheet of thawed puff pastry out and cut into 4 evenly sized strips.
Spread cream cheese over each strip

Arrange the cinnamon sugar apples on the edge of each strip, overlapping the edge slightly and overlapping each other. Carefully fold over the other half of the pastry and swiftly roll from one side to the other to make a tight roll of pastry and reveal a rose-like shape.
Place into well-greased muffin pans and bake on the lowest baking rack to prevent your apples from burning for 40â45 minutes until cooked through.
If they begin to catch simply cover with foil. Enjoy warm with an extra drizzle of honey.

ing: 110 g butter, melted, plus extra for brushing
650 g Woolworths Spicy Vegetables & Chickpea Medley, to serve
st: Place the milk, butter and mash in a bowl and whisk to combine.
Place the flour, salt, yeast, rosemary and sugar into the bowl of a stand mixer with the dough hook attached and mix to combine.
With the mixer running at low speed, add the milk mixture, then add the eggs.
Knead at a medium speed for 5â8 minutes, or until the dough pulls away from the sides of the bowl and is smooth and glossy.
Cover the bowl with a tea towel and prove in a warm spot until doubled in size, about 1 hour.
Lightly oil your hands and work surface and tip out the dough. Gently knock down.
Weigh out 11 x 100 g portions of dough and roll each portion into a neat ball.
Grease a 28 cm cast-iron pan or similar sized baking dish and place the dough balls inside. Brush with melted butter and sprinkle with salt. Prove uncovered for 15 minutes.
Bake at 180Â°C for 20â30 minutes, or until golden and cooked through.
Serve warm with Woolworths Spicy Vegetables & Chickpea Medley

t: Pulled Pork & Potato Salad With Slaw
ing: Avg. 900 g 4 seasoned pork cheek steaks
2 red onions, 1 onion sliced and 1 onion cut in eighths
30 g fresh Italian parsley, 1 /2 picked and 1 /2 finely chopped
st: Sign in/Register

ing: 100 g baby spinach, rocket & watercress salad
100 g plain South African feta cheese, crumbled
st: Sign in/Register

ing: 1 x 240 g Woolworths Easy to Bake Mexican Style Cornbread Kit
3 x 70 g cans Woolworths Soffritto Tomato Paste
st: Make the Mexican cornbread according to package instructions. Allow to cool enough to handle. Using a sharp bread knife, cut the loaf into 3 pieces lengthways.
To make the âSoweto sauceâ, place a cast-iron pan on the braai or on the stove.
Add the ghee and, once hot, add the shallots and a good pinch of salt.

Cook until translucent, then add the garlic. Cook for a further 3 minutes. Add the soffritto paste and cook over low heat for 30 minutes. Add a little water to loosen the sauce. Once the tomato paste is thick and rich, season with salt and set aside.

To cook the skilpadjies, prepare a small braai â charcoal is best. Once the coals are at a low heat, place the skilpadjies on the grid. Cook slowly until the caul fat is crispy and the filling is cooked through. Season with Maldon salt.

ing: 1 x 400 g can tomato & onion with sweet chilli braai relish
Sweet and sour gherkins, sliced, to serve
st: Lightly salt the onion slices and massage gently. This will reduce the intense onion flavour. Set them aside while preparing your burger.

Over medium heat coals (or a griddle pan over a medium heat on the stove), cook the burger patties for about 3 minutes or until a crust begins to form. Gently press down to give the patty more contact with the grill.
Before turning the patty over, generously brush the uncooked side with some mustard. Flip and cook the patty for another 3 minutes. The mustard is the secret step to a delicious crust on the patty.
Spoon the BBQ sauce onto the cooked side of the patty and add a slice of Emmental cheese. Allow the cheese to slowly melt.
Heat the tomato & onion braai relish over a medium heat until just simmering.

To assemble the burger, spoon some of the braai relish over the bottom half of your toasted bun followed by lettuce, gherkin slices and then the patty. Add a generous amount of salted onions before finishing with a drizzle of beefy mayonnaise,
Serve this juicy burger immediately with a side of napkins.

vegetable oil for frying

ing: 1 cup Woolworths Fresh Full Cream Milk
280 g Woolworths Self Raising Wheat Flour
100 g Lindt Excellence 70% Dark Chocolate, chopped
250 g Woolworths No Added Salt & Sugar Peanut Butter
st: Preheat the oven to 160Â°C and grease a 30 cm x 20 cm oval ovenproof dish and dust with cocoa powder. Lightly whisk together the milk, butter and eggs.

In another bowl, sift together the flour and cocoa, then stir in the sugar. Slowly add the milk mixture to the dry ingredients, beating until smooth. Fold through the chopped chocolate and pour into the dish.

t: Open chicken and garlic mayo sandwich
st: Preheat the oven to 180Â°C.
Place the garlic in the centre of a large sheet of foil, drizzle with the olive oil and wrap up. Roast for 40 minutes, then allow to cool.
Place the egg yolks and Dijon mustard in a mixing bowl. Squeeze the roast garlic into the bowl and mix with the egg and mustard.
Slowly pour in the oil, whisking continually, until the mayonnaise is pale and thick. Add the lemon juice and season to taste with salt. Add the celery and chicken and mix to combine.
Slice the warmed ciabatta and toast. Top with spoonfuls of the chicken mayonnaise and garnish with microherbs before serving.

ing: 100 g Kalamata olives, stoned, drained and halved lengthways
1â2 red onion, quartered and thinly sliced
130 g Woolworths marinated chargrilled artichokes, sliced into 2 cm pieces
50 g raw almonds, roughly chopped, to garnish
st: Melt the butter in a large nonstick saucepan and sauteÌ the couscous over a medium heat. Cook, stirring regularly, until the couscous is lightly toasted, about 5 minutes. Add the stock and bring to a boil.
Reduce the temperature to a simmer, cover and cook for 5 minutes, or until the couscous is just cooked.
Remove from the heat, cover and steam for a few minutes.
Tip into a bowl and stir. Allow to cool for about 5 minutes.
Mix the remaining ingredients, except the almonds and olive oil, with the cooked couscous and transfer to a serving dish.
Garnish with the almonds and drizzle with the olive oil.

ing: 340 g roasted red peppers in brine
st: Sign in/Register
Place the cornflakes in a bowl and add 100 g melted chocolate.
Mix well and press into a 24 cm greased tart pan.
Place the marshmallow eggs on top.
Whisk the cream into the remaining chocolate and pour over the tart making sure you reveal some of the eggs.
Chill for 2 hours until set.

ing: 70 g Black Kalamata and Green Treated Olives
100 g South African Grated Medium Fat Hard Cheese
st: Cook the spaghetti in boiling water for 10 minutes or until al dente, then drain.
While the pasta is cooling, heat the olive oil in a saucepan. Add the garlic and stir for 30 seconds over a medium heat.
Add the remaining ingredients except the cheese and seasoning. Simmer for 8 minutes. Check the seasoning - the anchovies will add saltiness.
Serve with pasta, Parmesan and garlic bread.

Place the butter and cream in a large saucepan. Once the butter has melted, add the powdered milk. Mix until it starts to thicken and pulls away from the side of the pan. Add the n food colouring if using. Mix in the icing sugar, then add the pistachios and cardamom and remove from the heat.
Roll tablespoonfuls of the mixture into balls while still a little warm. You should make approximately 18.

Once completely cool, dip into the white chocolate. Place on baking paper to allow to set.  Decorate with ground pistachios, rose petals and gold leaf. Refrigerate for up to a week in an airtight container.
